messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: customers on Dedicated pools (eu-west-1) may see throttled requests and elevated queueing for a subset of tenants after an autoscaler policy update at 08:12 UTC. Impact: ~3-5% of requests, higher for sustained high-concurrency tenants. Incident page: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/2865432100 :rotating_light:

harpreet: noticed sudden spike in pod churn and scale-down events. autoscaler metrics show an aggressive scale-down step triggered by short CPU dips. sample log:
````
autoscaler: scale_down_attempt cluster=dedicated-eu-west1 target=pool-a delta=-40 pods reason=cpu_below_threshold
kube: terminating pod worker-77 due to eviction
````

lucas: customers with long-running sessions hit queued requests as capacity dropped quickly and warm-pools were not primed. some requests retried with 429/504. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/dedicated/autoscale?from=now-30m&to=now

maria: rolling back autoscaler policy change and setting a cooldown. command: `opsctl autoscaler apply --region eu-west-1 --policy autoscale-safe-v1 --action rollback --cooldown 600s`

infra: mitigation steps applied:
- paused new autoscaler policy rollout across eu-west-1
- reverted to autoscale-safe-v1 on canary -> expanding to 100%
- set scale-down cooldown to 600s and min-ready pods to 3 per pool
- manually scaled up warm pool for flagged customers by +6 pods to absorb backlog
- temporarily relaxed per-tenant concurrency limits for affected tenants to allow graceful catch-up

harpreet: after rollback, queue length halved within 2m and retry errors reduced. p95 latency returning toward baseline. continuing to watch.

oncall: collecting affected tenant list and request ids to incident artifacts: s3://incidents/2865432100/artifacts. please avoid draining warmed nodes until we've captured heap/profile data.

support: drafting customer broadcast: "We detected transient request throttling on Dedicated pools in eu-west-1 due to an autoscaler policy update. We reverted the change and applied mitigations; affected customers should see recovery. Contact support if you continue to see throttling." Will send after 10m steady-state.

lucas: next steps: add autoscaler preflight that simulates scale-down decisions against historical short-burst traces, add an automatic rollback when scale_down_rate > 50% in 1m, and add a warm-pool priming check for Dedicated pools. Filing follow-ups ENG-15010 / OPS-15011 / QA-15012.

maria: planning controlled reintroduce of new autoscaler version with conservative thresholds and extended cooldowns, canary with synthetic load for 30m.

incident-bot: Incident page: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/2865432100 (runbook and artifacts). Broadcast to #customers-facing scheduled in 9m pending stability.

support: support team on watch. enterprise tenants flagged for direct outreach.

harpreet: closing note: metrics stable on rolled-back policy for 15m; we'll keep incident open for 30m post-stability then send final summary. if you see recurrence tag `@oncall` and upload logs to the artifacts folder. :white_check_mark:
